101	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
102	
103	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
104	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
105	
106	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
107	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
108	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
109	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
110	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
111	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
112	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
113	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
114	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
115	
116	## One-shot discipline (important)
117	
118	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
119	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
120	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
121	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
122	
123	## Pick the highest-value work
124	
125	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
126	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
127	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
128	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
129	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
130	
131	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
132	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
133	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
134	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
135	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
136	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
137	(it returns to the queue).
138	
139	## Fresh-context checkpoints
140	
141	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
142	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
143	checkpoints:
144	
145	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
146	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
147	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
148	  clean/build result.
149	
150	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
151	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
152	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
153	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
154	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
155	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
156	terminal `done` claim.
157	
158	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
159	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
160	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
161	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
162	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
163	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
164	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
165	
166	## Warnings are work
167	
168	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
169	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
170	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
171	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
172	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
173	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
174	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
175	why.
176	
177	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
178	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
179	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
180	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
181	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
182	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
183	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
184	
185	## Do the work (Lean)
186	
187	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
188	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
189	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
190	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
191	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
192	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
193	configured final build covers the same files.
194	
195	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
196	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
197	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
198	mathlib — query it:
199	
200	| You want | Use | Not |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
203	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
204	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
205	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
206	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
207	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
208	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
209	
210	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
211	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
212	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
213	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
214	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
215	back to grep.
216	
217	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
218	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
219	
220	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
221	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
222	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
223	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
224	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
225	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
226	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
227	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
228	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
229	
230	## Read the other projects
231	
232	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
233	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
234	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
235	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
236	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
237	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
238	
239	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
240	
241	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
242	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
243	needs no permission.
244	
245	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
246	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
247	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
248	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
249	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
250	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
251	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
252	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
253	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
254	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
255	
256	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
257	
258	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
259	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
260	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
261	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
262	
263	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
264	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
265	
266	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
267	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
268	  as **memory**.
269	
270	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
271	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
272	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
273	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
274	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
275	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
276	shorter. This pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
277	
278	## Resuming after an interruption
279	
280	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
281	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
282	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
283	
284	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
285	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
286	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
287	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
288	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
289	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
290	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
291	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
292	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
293	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
294	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
295	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
296	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
297	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
298	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
299	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
300	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
301	
302	## Final report (your last message)
303	
304	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
305	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
306	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
307	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
308	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
309	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
310	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
311	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
312	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
313	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
314	not by itself a reason to stop.
315	
316	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
317	
318	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
319	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
320	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
321	`subagents` skill):
322	
323	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
324	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
325	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
326	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
327	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
328	
329	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/

    (by

      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R

      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])

  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SupportTube
7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Finite
8	
9	/-!
10	# The support-tube finiteness engine: the (c1)-finite production brick (G-4)
11	
12	The algebraic half of the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) (`informal/w4-g4-worksheet.md`
13	§3, the one row with no landed engine): for a divisor adaptation over a test ring `R`,
14	the chart-local colength `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is a **finite** `R`-module — Kleiman's
15	finiteness-of-the-divisor-subscheme step, per piece.
16	
17	## The honest hypothesis (probe finding)
18	
19	The colength is the section ring of the piece trace of the family support
20	(`supportLocus_inter_pieces`): the closed subscheme of the affine piece `D(h_j)` cut by
21	`f_j`, whose underlying set is `D(h_j) \ D(f_j) = supportLocus ∩ D(h_j)`.  The engine
22	input is that this trace is **closed in the whole relative curve**; universal closedness
23	of the curve over the base (the landed licence `instIsProperRelCurveHom`) then makes the
24	trace universally closed over `Spec R`, and a universally closed affine morphism of
25	finite type is finite (`IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom` +
26	`IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType` — the mathlib heart, the
27	`SlicingFlatKernel` luck again).  No Noetherian hypothesis anywhere.
28	
29	Fibrewise finiteness data alone (each fibre colength artinian, even of constant total
30	dimension) canNOT replace the closed-trace input.  Guard examples:
31	
32	* `Γ(𝔸¹) = k[x]` over `k` with `f = 0`: excluded by `[UniversallyClosed]` on the
33	  structure morphism (the affine line is not proper).
34	* the hyperbola `k[t,x]⧸(tx−1)` over `k[t]` inside `X = ℙ¹_{k[t]}`, piece the affine
35	  chart: every fibre colength is artinian, the module is even flat, yet not finite —
36	  the closure of the trace leaks into `(∞, t=0)`, so the closed-trace hypothesis fails
37	  exactly where it must.
38	* two disjoint base sections with a piece missing one point of one section: piece
39	  colength `k[t] × k[t,t⁻¹]`, all fibre colengths artinian of constant total dimension
40	  `2` on the glued module — the PER-PIECE trace leaks.  Hence the certificate's
41	  per-piece clause genuinely constrains the adaptation, and the fibrewise input of
42	  P-fib-N enters this brick only through its topological shadow, the **no-leak fibre
43	  criterion** threaded below (`hfib` of
44	  `finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset`).
45	
46	## Main declarations
47	
48	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLeak` — the leak locus of a support trace out of an
49	  open `U`: `closure (supportLocus ∩ U) \ U`, closed
50	  (`isClosed_supportLeak`), with `isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`
51	  and the fibre criterion `supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre`;
52	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_image_supportLeak` — the tube-side product: the base
53	  image of the leak locus is closed under a universally closed structure morphism, so
54	  its complement is the Zariski-open base locus where the trace is closed;
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed` — **the
56	  abstract engine**: `V` affine open in `X` over `Spec R`, structure morphism
57	  universally closed and locally of finite type, `V \ D(g)` closed in `X` ⟹
58	  `Γ(X, V) ⧸ (g)` is a finite `R`-module (via the closed immersion
59	  `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ (g)) ⟶ X` and mathlib's integral = universally closed + affine);
60	* `DivisorAdaptation.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter` /
61	  `finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty` /
62	  `finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset` /
63	  `finite_colength_of_supportLocus_subset` — **the (c1)-finite clause** for the piece
64	  `j`, in the closed-trace, leak-locus, fibrewise no-leak, and dominant-piece
65	  spellings.  CertUniv consumes the fibrewise form with `hfib` produced from the seed
66	  design + P-fib-N fibre data, or the closed-trace form directly.
67	
68	The `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through the
69	`Over` structure (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate the same
70	instances.
71	-/
72	
73	set_option autoImplicit false
74	
75	universe u
76	
77	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
78	
79	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
80	
81	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
82	
83	/-! ## The leak locus of a support trace -/
84	
85	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
86	
87	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)
88	
89	/-- **The leak locus of a support trace**: the part of the closure of
90	`supportLocus ∩ U` that escapes `U`.  The trace `supportLocus ∩ U` is closed in `X`
91	iff the leak locus is empty (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`);
92	its base image under a universally closed structure morphism is closed
93	(`isClosed_image_supportLeak`), so the trace is closed over the complementary base
94	open — the Zariski-local piece-isolation mechanism of the DDR-4 finiteness input. -/
95	def supportLeak (U : X.Opens) : Set X :=
96	  closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) \ (U : Set X)
97	
98	lemma isClosed_supportLeak (U : X.Opens) : IsClosed (d.supportLeak U) :=
99	  isClosed_closure.sdiff U.isOpen
100	
101	/-- The leak locus lies in the support outside the open: leaks are support points. -/
102	lemma supportLeak_subset_sdiff (U : X.Opens) :
103	    d.supportLeak U ⊆ d.supportLocus \ (U : Set X) := fun _ hx =>
104	  ⟨closure_minimal Set.inter_subset_left d.isClosed_supportLocus hx.1, hx.2⟩
105	
106	/-- The support trace on an open is closed in the whole space iff nothing leaks. -/
107	lemma isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (U : X.Opens) :
108	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) ↔ d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
109	  constructor
110	  · intro h
111	    rw [supportLeak, h.closure_eq, Set.sdiff_eq_empty]
112	    exact Set.inter_subset_right
113	  · intro h
114	    rw [supportLeak, Set.sdiff_eq_empty] at h
115	    exact isClosed_of_closure_subset fun x hx =>
116	      ⟨closure_minimal Set.inter_subset_left d.isClosed_supportLocus hx, h hx⟩
117	
118	/-- **The fibre no-leak criterion** — the named threading slot for the fibrewise data
119	of the (c1)-finite clause: if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the
120	trace stays inside `U`, the leak locus is empty.  In the CertUniv instantiation the
121	hypothesis is produced from the seed design and the P-fib-N fibre analysis (the fibre
122	support is a finite set of pairwise-incomparable closed points, each isolated inside
123	its piece). -/
124	lemma supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre (f : X ⟶ S) {U : X.Opens}
125	    (hfib : ∀ s : S, f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X))
126	      ⊆ (U : Set X)) :
127	    d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
128	  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
129	  rintro x ⟨hxc, hxU⟩
130	  exact hxU (hfib (f.base x) ⟨rfl, hxc⟩)
131	
132	/-- **The base image of the leak locus is closed** under a universally closed morphism
133	(the properness licence): its complement is the Zariski-open locus of the base over
134	which the support trace on `U` is closed — the tube-side mechanism for producing the
135	closed-trace input Zariski-locally on the base. -/
136	theorem isClosed_image_supportLeak (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] (U : X.Opens) :
137	    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLeak U) :=
138	  f.isClosedMap _ (d.isClosed_supportLeak U)
139	
140	end Scheme.LocalEquations
141	
142	/-! ## The abstract finiteness engine -/
143	
144	namespace IsAffineOpen
145	
146	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
147	
148	/-- The underlying set of the closed subscheme of an affine open cut by an ideal of its
149	section ring, embedded in the ambient scheme: `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ Spec Γ(X, V) ⟶ X`
150	has range the vanishing set of `I` on `V`. -/
151	lemma range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec (I : Ideal Γ(X, V)) :
152	    Set.range ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
153	      = X.zeroLocus (I : Set Γ(X, V)) ∩ (V : Set X) := by
154	  have hcomp : ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
155	      = ⇑hV.fromSpec ∘ ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) := by
156	    ext x
157	    exact Scheme.Hom.comp_apply _ _ x
158	  have hq : Set.range ⇑(Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))
159	      = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set Γ(X, V)) := by
160	    have h := range_comap_of_surjective _ _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective (I := I))
161	    rw [Ideal.mk_ker] at h
162	    exact h
163	  rw [hcomp, Set.range_comp, hq]
164	  exact hV.fromSpec_image_zeroLocus _
165	
166	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
167	
168	/-- **The structure triangle of the chart-local closed subscheme**: composing
169	`Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ X` with the structure morphism is `Spec` of the structure map
170	`R → Γ(X, V) ⧸ I` (the `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` algebra, quotient structure). -/
171	lemma specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over (I : Ideal Γ(X, V)) :
172	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec
173	        ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
174	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I))) := by
175	  have h1 : hV.fromSpec ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
176	      = Spec.map ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of R)).inv

11	/-!
12	# The support tube: the family support is closed over the base (DDR-4 finiteness input)
13	
14	The geometric half of the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
15	item 4): for a local-equation system `d` on a scheme `X`, the **support locus** — the
16	set of points where the (well-defined, by the ratio law) germ of the local equation is
17	not a unit — is closed in `X`; over a base `S` with `X → S` universally closed (the
18	standing `IsProper C.hom`, base-changed to the relative curve over every test ring),
19	its image in `S` is closed, and the **tube lemma** holds: if the support fibre over a
20	base point `s` is contained in an open `U` (e.g. a union of adaptation pieces), then so
21	is the whole support over a Zariski neighbourhood of `s` — piece isolation Zariski-locally
22	on the base.
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset` — the topological tube core: a
27	  closed map, a closed set `T`, an open `U` containing the `T`-fibre over `y` ⟹ an open
28	  neighbourhood `V ∋ y` with `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T ⊆ U` (via `Set.kernImage`);
29	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.unitLocus` / `supportLocus` — the (open) locus where the
30	  equations are germwise units, and its closed complement;
31	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ` — membership reads on ANY
32	  covering member through the ratio law;
33	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLocus_inter_opens` — the per-member trace
34	  `supp ∩ U_x = U_x \ D(eqn x)`;
35	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_image_supportLocus`,
36	  `Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` — closed image and the tube, for any
37	  `f : X ⟶ S` with `[UniversallyClosed f]`;
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperRelSndLeft`, `instIsProperRelCurveHom` — **the
39	  licence**: `IsProper C.hom` base-changes to the relative curve over an arbitrary test
40	  ring `R` (the field-keyed instances of `Curve/BaseChangeInstances` generalised), so
41	  `UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution;
42	* `DivisorAdaptation.mem_basicOpen_eqn_of_mem_unitLocus` / `unitLocus_eq` /
43	  `supportLocus_inter_pieces` — the adaptation reads the SAME support: on a piece,
44	  `d`'s support trace is `D(h_j) \ D(f_j)` (through `eqn_rel`, both ways);
45	* `FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces` — the pieces' section rings are `R`-flat;
46	* `DivisorAdaptation.flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` /
47	  `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — **the (c1) junction**: a
48	  fibrewise-regular adaptation equation has flat colength over the Noetherian test
49	  ring (the `SlicingFlat` keystone on the piece ring), and a finite colength (the
50	  support-tube finiteness input) is then projective — the two clauses of
51	  `IsCertified` (c1) for the piece `j`.
52	-/

62	/-! ## The topological tube core -/
63	
64	section TubeCore
65	
66	variable {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
67	
68	/-- **The closed-map tube lemma**: for a closed map `f`, a closed `T ⊆ X` and an open
69	`U ⊆ X`, if the `T`-fibre over `y` is contained in `U` then so is `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T` for some
70	open neighbourhood `V` of `y`. Take `V := Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ)`, open by
71	`isClosedMap_iff_kernImage`. -/
72	theorem IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset {f : X → Y}
73	    (hf : IsClosedMap f) {T U : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hU : IsOpen U) {y : Y}
74	    (hfib : f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ T ⊆ U) :
75	    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ y ∈ V ∧ f ⁻¹' V ∩ T ⊆ U := by
76	  refine ⟨Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ),
77	    isClosedMap_iff_kernImage.mp hf (hU.union hT.isOpen_compl), ?_, ?_⟩
78	  · intro x hx
79	    by_cases hxT : x ∈ T
80	    · exact Or.inl (hfib ⟨hx, hxT⟩)
81	    · exact Or.inr hxT
82	  · rintro x ⟨hxV, hxT⟩
83	    rcases hxV (rfl : f x = f x) with h | h
84	    · exact h
85	    · exact absurd hxT h
86	
87	end TubeCore

93	/-! ## The support locus of a local-equation system -/
94	
95	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
96	
97	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)
98	
99	/-- **The unit locus** of a local-equation system: the (open) union of the basic opens
100	of the equations — the locus where the divisor cut by `d` is trivial. -/
101	def unitLocus : X.Opens := ⨆ x, X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)
102	
103	lemma basicOpen_le_unitLocus (x : X) : X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) ≤ d.unitLocus :=
104	  le_iSup (fun x => X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)) x
105	
106	/-- Membership in the unit locus reads on ANY covering member containing the point:
107	`y ∈ unitLocus` iff the germ of `eqn x` at `y` is a unit, for every member `x` with
108	`y ∈ cover.opens x` (well-definedness across members is the ratio law). -/
109	lemma mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
110	    y ∈ d.unitLocus
111	      ↔ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) := by
112	  constructor
113	  · intro h
114	    obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp h
115	    have hy' : y ∈ d.cover.opens x' := X.basicOpen_le _ hx'
116	    have hu' : IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x') y hy').hom (d.eqn x')) :=
117	      (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy').mp hx'
118	    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := d.ratio_isUnit x x'
119	    have hyW : y ∈ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x' := ⟨hy, hy'⟩
120	    have h := congrArg
121	      ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x') y hyW).hom) hu
122	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
123	    rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
124	    exact ⟨u.isUnit.map _, hu'⟩
125	  · intro h
126	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x, (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr h⟩
127	
128	/-- **The support locus** of a local-equation system: the closed set of points where
129	the (well-defined) germ of the local equation fails to be a unit — the underlying set
130	of the divisor cut by `d`. -/
131	def supportLocus : Set X := (d.unitLocus : Set X)ᶜ
132	
133	lemma isClosed_supportLocus : IsClosed d.supportLocus :=
134	  d.unitLocus.isOpen.isClosed_compl
135	
136	lemma mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
137	    y ∈ d.supportLocus
138	      ↔ ¬ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) :=
139	  not_congr (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy)
140	
141	/-- **The per-member trace of the support**: on a covering member, the support locus is
142	the member minus the basic open of its equation. -/
143	lemma supportLocus_inter_opens (x : X) :
144	    d.supportLocus ∩ (d.cover.opens x : Set X)
145	      = (d.cover.opens x : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) : Set X) := by
146	  ext y
147	  constructor
148	  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hy⟩
149	    refine ⟨hy, fun hyb => hsupp (d.basicOpen_le_unitLocus x hyb)⟩
150	  · rintro ⟨hy, hyb⟩
151	    refine ⟨fun hyU => hyb ?_, hy⟩
152	    exact (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy).mp hyU)
153	
154	/-- **The support is closed over the base**: the image of the support locus under a
155	universally closed morphism (e.g. the structure morphism of the relative curve, from
156	the standing `IsProper C.hom`) is closed. -/
157	theorem isClosed_image_supportLocus (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] :
158	    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLocus) :=
159	  f.isClosedMap _ d.isClosed_supportLocus
160	
161	/-- **The support tube** (piece isolation, Zariski-locally on the base): for a
162	universally closed `f : X ⟶ S`, if the support fibre over a base point `s` is contained
163	in an open `U` (a union of adaptation pieces, in the DDR-4 instantiation), then there
164	is a Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `s` such that the whole support over `V` is contained
165	in `U`. -/
166	theorem exists_supportTube (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X}
167	    (hU : IsOpen U) {s : S} (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
168	    ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧ f.base ⁻¹' (V : Set S) ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
169	  obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hsV, hV⟩ := (f.isClosedMap).exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset
170	    d.isClosed_supportLocus hU hfib
171	  exact ⟨⟨V, hVopen⟩, hsV, hV⟩
172	
173	end Scheme.LocalEquations

175	/-! ## The licence: properness of the relative curve over an arbitrary test ring -/
176	
177	section RelCurveProper
178	
179	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
180	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
181	
182	/-- **Base change of properness to an arbitrary test ring**: the second projection of
183	`C ⊗ Spec R` is proper, for every commutative `k`-algebra `R` — the general-`R` form of
184	`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.instIsProperSndLeft` (which is keyed on field extensions).
185	This is the DDR-4 support-tube licence over the `Z(♦)`-chart rings `R_Z`. -/
186	instance instIsProperRelSndLeft : IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left :=
187	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsProper)
188	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
189	
190	/-- The properness instance, keyed on the `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` spelling installed by
191	`relCurve.instOver` (definitionally the second projection). In particular
192	`UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution, which is what
193	`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` consumes. -/
194	instance instIsProperRelCurveHom :
195	    IsProper ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) :=
196	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left)
197	
198	/-- Acceptance smoke test: the support tube applies to the relative curve over an
199	arbitrary test ring with the universally-closed instance found by resolution. -/
200	private theorem supportTube_smoke (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
201	    {U : Set (relCurve C R)} (hU : IsOpen U) {s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)}
202	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus
203	      ⊆ U) :
204	    ∃ V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).Opens, s ∈ V ∧
205	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' (V : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
206	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U :=
207	  d.exists_supportTube _ hU hfib
208	
209	end RelCurveProper

213	section Adaptation
214	
215	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
216	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
217	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k}
218	
219	namespace FinCoverData
220	
221	variable [IsFinite π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
222	
223	/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring**: each `Γ(D(h_j))` is a
224	localization of a pinned-chart ring, which is free over `R`; the `FinCoverData`
225	companion of `ThetaGeneratorSeed.flat_sections_piece`. -/
226	theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
227	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) := by
228	  cases j with
229	  | inl j =>
230	      exact flat_sections_basicOpen R (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
231	        (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π false) (D.h₀ j)
232	  | inr j =>
233	      exact flat_sections_basicOpen R (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
234	        (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π true) (D.h₁ j)
235	
236	end FinCoverData

238	namespace DivisorAdaptation
239	
240	variable [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
241	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
242	
243	/-- On a piece, the germ of the adaptation equation is a unit iff the germ of `d`'s
244	tautological equation is (the pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel`, read at germs). -/
245	lemma isUnit_germ_eqn_iff (j : A.index) {w : relCurve C R} (hwj : w ∈ A.pieces j) :
246	    IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) w hwj).hom (A.eqn j))
247	      ↔ IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens w) w
248	          (d.cover.mem_opens w)).hom (d.eqn w)) := by
249	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j w
250	  have hwW : w ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens w := ⟨hwj, d.cover.mem_opens w⟩
251	  have h := congrArg
252	    (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens w) w hwW).hom) hu
253	  rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
254	  rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
255	  exact and_iff_right (u.isUnit.map _)
256	
257	/-- On a piece, membership in `d`'s unit locus is membership in the basic open of the
258	adaptation equation. -/
259	lemma mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus (j : A.index) {w : relCurve C R}
260	    (hwj : w ∈ A.pieces j) :
261	    w ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) ↔ w ∈ d.unitLocus := by
262	  rw [(relCurve C R).mem_basicOpen _ w hwj, A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hwj]
263	  exact (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens w)).symm
264	
265	/-- The adaptation's basic opens land in `d`'s unit locus. -/
266	lemma basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus (j : A.index) :
267	    (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) ≤ d.unitLocus := fun _ hw =>
268	  (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j
269	    ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.eqn j) hw)).mp hw
270	
271	/-- **The adaptation computes the unit locus**: the union of the basic opens of the
272	adaptation equations IS `d`'s unit locus (so the adaptation and the system cut the same
273	support). Uses that the pieces cover the relative curve (`exists_mem_pieces`). -/
274	lemma iSup_basicOpen_eqn_eq_unitLocus :
275	    (⨆ j, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j)) = d.unitLocus := by
276	  refine le_antisymm (iSup_le fun j => A.basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus j) ?_
277	  intro w hw
278	  obtain ⟨j, hwj⟩ := A.toFinCoverData.exists_mem_pieces w
279	  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨j, (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j hwj).mpr hw⟩
280	
281	/-- **The per-piece trace of the family support**: on the piece `D(h_j)`, the support
282	locus of the family is exactly `D(h_j) \ D(f_j)` — the underlying set of the colength
283	`Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`. This is the shape the DDR-4 finiteness argument consumes: the
284	piece trace of the globally closed (and, over the base, properly closed) support. -/
285	lemma supportLocus_inter_pieces (j : A.index) :
286	    d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
287	      = (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
288	        \ ((relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
289	  ext w
290	  constructor
291	  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hwj⟩
292	    exact ⟨hwj, fun hwb => hsupp (A.basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus j hwb)⟩
293	  · rintro ⟨hwj, hwb⟩
294	    exact ⟨fun hwU => hwb ((A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j hwj).mpr hwU), hwj⟩
295	
296	end DivisorAdaptation

300	/-! ### The (c1) junction: flat, then finite projective, colengths -/
301	
302	section Junction
303	
304	variable [IsFinite π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
305	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
306	
307	/-- **The (c1) flatness clause from fibrewise regularity** (the `SlicingFlat` keystone
308	on the piece ring): if the adaptation equation `f_j` is a nonzerodivisor in every
309	residue-field fibre `Γ(D(h_j)) ⊗ κ(p)`, then the chart-local colength
310	`Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is flat over the Noetherian test ring. The fibrewise hypothesis is
311	the seed's `fibre_regular` clause transported through `eqn_rel` (the I-0203 open
312	transport item). -/
313	theorem flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField [IsNoetherianRing R]
314	    (j : A.index)
315	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
316	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
317	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
318	        nonZeroDivisors
319	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
320	    Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := by
321	  haveI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) :=
322	    A.toFinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces j
323	  exact Module.Flat.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField hfib
324	
325	/-- **The certificate clause (c1) for the piece `j`**: fibrewise-regular equation +
326	finite colength (the support-tube finiteness input) ⟹ the colength is finite
327	projective over the Noetherian test ring — `IsCertified.finite_colength` and
328	`IsCertified.projective_colength` at `j`. -/
329	theorem projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField [IsNoetherianRing R]
330	    (j : A.index)
331	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
332	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
333	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
334	        nonZeroDivisors
335	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
336	    [Module.Finite R (A.colength j)] :
337	    Module.Projective R (A.colength j) := by
338	  haveI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) :=
339	    A.toFinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces j
340	  exact Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField hfib
341	
342	end Junction

11	# The support tube in `Away`-chart form
12	
13	The pointwise certificate gate (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`) asks, at each base prime
14	`p`, for an element `r ∉ p` such that the pulled system is certified over
15	`Localization.Away r`.  The support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
16	delivers piece isolation over an *abstract* Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `p`.  This file
17	refines that neighbourhood to a basic open — the shape `Localization.Away` needs — and
18	records the resulting statement.
19	
20	The refinement is the standard fact that basic opens form a topological basis of
21	`Spec R` (`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`); the content is only that the tube's
22	conclusion is monotone in the neighbourhood, so shrinking `V` to a basic open inside it
23	preserves support isolation.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportTube` — the tube with a
28	  basic-open neighbourhood: an `r ∉ p` whose basic open isolates the support inside `U`.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` — the same for the
30	  relative curve over a test ring, with the properness licence supplied.
31	-/
32	
33	set_option autoImplicit false
34	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
35	
36	universe u
37	
38	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
43	
44	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
45	
46	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (d : X.LocalEquations)
47	
48	/-- **The support tube with a basic-open neighbourhood.** If the support fibre over a base
49	prime `p` lies inside an open `U`, then some `r ∉ p` has its whole basic-open preimage's
50	support inside `U`.
51	
52	The tube produces an abstract neighbourhood; basic opens are a basis of `Spec R`
53	(`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`), so shrinking to a basic open inside it keeps the
54	conclusion by monotonicity of the preimage. This is the form the `Localization.Away`
55	charts of `IsLocallyCertified` consume. -/
56	theorem exists_basicOpen_supportTube (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
57	    [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
58	    (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
59	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
60	      f.base ⁻¹' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
61	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
62	  obtain ⟨V, hpV, hV⟩ := d.exists_supportTube f hU hfib
63	  -- refine `V` to a basic open around `p`
64	  obtain ⟨W, hWmem, hpW, hWV⟩ :=
65	    PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open
66	      (a := p) hpV V.isOpen
67	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hWmem
68	  exact ⟨r, (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen r p).mp hpW,
69	    fun x hx => hV ⟨hWV hx.1, hx.2⟩⟩
70	
71	end Scheme.LocalEquations
72	
73	/-! ## The relative-curve form -/
74	
75	section RelCurve
76	
77	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
78	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
79	
80	/-- **The relative-curve support tube, basic-open form.** For a local-equation system on
81	the relative curve over a test ring, fibrewise containment of the support in an open `U`

87	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) {U : Set (relCurve C R)} (hU : IsOpen U)
88	    {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
89	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
90	        {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
91	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
92	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
93	          (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
94	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U :=
95	  d.exists_basicOpen_supportTube _ hU hfib
96	
97	end RelCurve
98	
99	/-! ## No-leak over a shrunken base, from one fibre
100	
101	The point of the tube in the certificate lane: the no-leak hypothesis that is false
102	globally becomes *true over the tube*, because the support over the tube is already inside
103	the piece — so its closure is too, and the fibre clause holds for every base point of the

105	
106	section NoLeakOverTube
107	
108	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
109	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
110	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
111	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
112	
113	namespace DivisorAdaptation
114	
115	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
116	
117	omit [IsProper C.hom]
118	
119	/-- **Support containment upgrades to the fibrewise no-leak clause.** If the whole family
120	support lies in the piece `j`, then over every base point the fibre of the *closure* of the
121	piece trace stays in the piece: the trace is then all of the support, which is closed.
122	
123	This is the bridge between what the tube delivers (support containment over a shrunken
124	base) and what the certificate assembler consumes (the fibrewise clause of
125	`finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset`). -/
126	theorem forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLocus_subset (j : A.index)
127	    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
128	    ∀ s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R),
129	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
130	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
131	        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
132	  intro s x hx
133	  have htrace : d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) = d.supportLocus :=
134	    Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub
135	  rw [htrace, d.isClosed_supportLocus.closure_eq] at hx
136	  exact hsub hx.2
137	
138	/-- The no-leak clause for **every** piece, from containment of the support in each: the
139	exact `hnoLeak` input of the certificate assemblers
140	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`,
141	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`). -/
142	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_supportLocus_subset
143	    (hsub : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
144	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)),
145	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
146	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
147	        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
148	  fun j => A.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLocus_subset j (hsub j)
149	
150	end DivisorAdaptation
151	
152	end NoLeakOverTube
153	
154	/-! ## The tube-fibre reduction
155	
156	Combining the two halves: to obtain the certificate assembler's `hnoLeak` input over an
157	`Away` chart, it is enough to check at ONE base prime that the support fibre lies in an
158	open — the tube spreads it to a basic-open neighbourhood, and containment there upgrades to
159	the fibrewise clause. This is the precise statement the remaining geometric work has to
160	feed, and it mentions only a single fibre. -/
161	
162	section TubeFibre
163	
164	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
165	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
166	
167	/-- **The tube-fibre reduction.** If at a base prime `p` the support fibre of the system
168	lies inside an open `U`, then some `r ∉ p` has the entire support over `D(r)` inside `U`.
169	
170	Stated so that the remaining certificate obligation is *purely fibrewise*: check one fibre,
171	get a Zariski chart.  The consumer chain is
172	`exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` → the pulled system's support over `D(r)` →
173	`DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_supportLocus_subset` → the assembler's
174	`hnoLeak`, and then `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`
175	consumes the resulting away-certificate. -/
176	theorem exists_away_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre_subset
177	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).Opens) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
178	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
179	        {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ (U : Set (relCurve C R))) :
180	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
181	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹'
182	          (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) ∩ d.supportLocus
183	        ⊆ (U : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
184	  exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre C R d U.isOpen hfib
185	
186	end TubeFibre
187	
188	end AlgebraicGeometry

  "title": "Base-change twists and descend the finite-field atlas",
  "summary": "*** PROTECTION CONFLICT, flagged review-ajcr r7 (2026-07-30). THE SECOND HALF OF THIS ROW PRESCRIBES A ROUTE HUMAN DECISION I-0492 FORBIDS. Read this before claiming; the row is pending, hence claimable, and its text points a prover at work no lane may do. ***

WHAT IS FORBIDDEN. The sentence 'transport P1 automorphisms and fixed-twist divisor charts across scalar extension, equip the outer atlas with semilinear Galois descent data, and descend it ... depends on the twist-atlas architecture' names exactly the two things I-0492 clause 1 rules out: the GL_2(k)/Aut(P1) action on P1 (twistedP1Map = pi >> P1.autOfMatrix, TwistedFiberTwoCover.lean:29 / P1Aut.lean:227), and descent work whose only purpose is to rescue R1. The leaf it depends on, twist-atlas, is REJECTED on precisely that ground. So a rejected leaf's architecture is still being prescribed by a claimable row.

WHY IT SURVIVED: this row's priority was lowered high -> low, but the SUMMARY was never edited. A lane reads the text, not the priority field.

WHAT REMAINS LEGITIMATE, and it is the first sentence only: assemble the finite-field avoidance endpoint -- transport the residue support into P1(k), combine image-ncard injectivity with the ncard <= g bound and the finite-cardinality P1 theorem (finite-field-avoid.cardinality, DONE), and spread the resulting fibre containment to a support tube. That half needs no twist and no descent. Its two sibling inputs are done.

THE LIVE ROUTE INSTEAD OF THE OUTER ATLAS is R2/widened: IsLocallyCertifiedAff, DivFamZarAff and divFunctorAff take (C, R, n) and NO pi (DivisorFamilyAffZar.lean:103, :165; DivisorFamilyAffMap.lean:290), so the twist quantifier DISAPPEARS rather than needing an atlas to absorb it. Live work over that carrier is the classifier (framecover-aff, fieldmono-aff).

STATUS left pending and priority left low deliberately: the legitimate first half is real work, and nothing here is claimed."

  "summary": "*** THIS ROW IS NOW THE EXPOSED ANTECEDENT (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). Not because anything
here changed -- because the item next to it was discharged and this one was behind it. ***

ajcr-p4 discharged the chart-finiteness (hlft) antecedent at the real atlas (Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean;
audited by me, it is a real discharge and not a relocation -- see AJCR.w4-rep's arithmetic
correction). JacobianData has FOUR fields, and with hlft gone the finiteness side of the datum is
down to ONE open input, which is this row's: quasiCompact.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE BLURRED, and it is why the freeness next door does not help here:
 * PER-CHART compactness is FREE at the carrier the divisor-representability lane returns
   (compactSpace_divScheme, DivSchemeQProj.lean) -- DivScheme is a closed subscheme of the compact
   Grassmannian pair.
 * CompactSpace of the GLUED object is NOT, and it is what JacobianData needs. For the
   class-indexed atlas the index type is infinite, so the finite route JacobianData.ofCharts
   ([Finite iota] + per-chart compactness) IS UNAVAILABLE, and ofChartsOfCompactSpace takes the
   glued compactness directly.
Anyone quoting "compactness is free at the carrier" for the glued form is making exactly the
conflation this note exists to prevent. ajcr-p4 stated the distinction correctly in their own file;
keep it.

SO THE ROUTE IS THIS ROW'S ROUTE, unchanged and now unavoidable: quasi-compactness comes from the
ABEL IMAGE (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage), never from the construction. The row's own analysis
below is intact and its correction-at-the-top is honest about what "discharged" was wrong about.

WHY THE all-children-done WARNING STAYS: recorded in I-0971 and unchanged -- degwindow being done
does not close this row, which owes the image argument. Do not let a janitor set it done.

DAT-J: JacobianData assembly -- quasi-compactness via the Abel image of Div^g-lite.

*** CORRECTION AT THE TOP, 2026-07-29 (run 0071 s0016 close, ajcr-divrep), against MY OWN header
below. A fresh-context audit (I-0799/I-0800/I-0802/I-0803) refuted three of its claims. Commit
9753ad6e3; the Lean is unchanged and still kernel-green, the PRICING was wrong.

WHAT SURVIVES: the effectivity half is genuinely divRep-FREE (the audit cone-checked 323 files:
no divRepClassify, no DivRepAffinePullback, no IsChartClause, no universal family), and the three
theorems are real, sorry-free, rooted and axiom-clean.

WHAT IS REFUTED -- and it is the word "discharged":
 (1) I called exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero a SATISFIABILITY PROBE and claimed the
     degree map hits g "unconditionally on the curve". FALSE, arithmetically: CurveDivisor.deg is
     weighted by residue degrees (Divisor.lean:61), so its image is index*Z. On a genus-1 curve of
     index 3 over Q no divisor of degree 1 = g exists and the theorem is a VACUOUS TRUTH. The
     campaign reference does not escape it: deg (m . fiberWeilDivisor) = m*delta (WindowLedger:133)
     requires delta | g. So the face RELOCATES the hypothesis (Z is an ARGUMENT), it does not
     discharge it. Exactly the reduction-to-a-possibly-false-hypothesis trap this project has
     recorded twice -- passes every census because it IS then a theorem.
 (2) THE BINDING LIMIT IS NOT THE DESCENT ONE I DISCLOSED. Since the splitting field L is
     existential inside the proof, the reference binder is UNIFORM: forall L, deg L (Zof L) = g,
     over every extension including L = k. Strictly stronger than the degree-0 face asks, and it
     has NO PRODUCER anywhere in the tree.
 (3) THE CONE IS NOT Challenge-FREE, which w4-datj 0.5/3.4 make BINDING for a DAT-J producer:
     DivisorDatumRankOne -> Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance:6 -> Challenge. So "available today"
     does NOT mean "consumable by DJ-2/DJ-3 today". Separately: 0.5's own claim that FLVClass is
     Challenge-free is also false at HEAD (Degree.lean:7 -> ChiCurve -> Challenge), so the standing
     "never riemann_inequality_curve" rule no longer avoids the cycle. Tree-wide, pre-existing,
     and it needs its own decision.
 (4) A docstring advertised PicRepDatum.exists_effective_deg_eq_at_point, which DOES NOT EXIST.
     So the one face that would consume the Pic^0 universal property is absent; lam/hlam remain
     caller-supplied.

SO THE HONEST STATE OF THE EFFECTIVITY HALF: divRep-free, and CONDITIONAL on an arithmetic
hypothesis about the curve's index that nothing produces. Not discharged.

WHAT DAT-J OWES NOW: (a) a degree-g divisor over the relevant field -- an index condition, newly
visible and genuinely open; (b) descent from the splitting field to kappa(y) (dat-g); (c) the Abel
square at an INDEPENDENTLY PINNED pt (the s0012 retraction stands); (d) a PicRepDatum from DAT-G
(divRep-gated); (e) a Challenge-free route for the whole producer cone. DJ-0 remains landed.

THE HEADLINE, WITH ITS OWN CORRECTION FIRST. I originally called this a REPRICING -- 'at genus 0 the degree condition is provably idle'. A fresh-context audit refuted that (I-1650, I-1653) and I accepted it in eb-series commit 33cb26bae1. The truth: at genus 0, for every T and every lam, the antecedent of hrig and membership in pic0Subgroup are EQUIVALENT, so hrig is hvan with the same predicate spelled '= 1' rather than 'deg = 0'. The degree left the NOTATION, not the mathematics. The tell was in my own file: the converse needs no genus hypothesis, and a genuinely weaker target does not round-trip for free.

WHAT IS THEREFORE TRUE AND USEFUL:
 (a) pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity -- hvan at EVERY test object is one hypothesis with field-point rigidity of picEt, both directions. The gain is STATABILITY: classDeg carries five fibre binders (all five measured as genuinely required, one dying at 20000 heartbeats) that do not synthesize through the relCurve def barrier, and the triviality spelling needs none of them. So hypotheses that could not be STATED at a general prime become statable.
 (b) rigidity_iff_rigidityAff -- the test-object quantifier drops: the vanishing follows from a hypothesis with NO SCHEME in it, only k-algebras, plus classes, and algebra maps into fields, and that form is NOT stronger (converse landed after the audit pointed out my caveat left it unproved). jacobianData_of_rigidityAff composes to the goal object; the P1 forms discharge the genus.
 (c) fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup -- the reusable half, general in the test; pic-g's ring-level engine work consumes it.
 (d) Pic0RingDatumEngine -- at genus 0 the RE-4 rigid engine's fibrewise hypothesis is FREE (witness: the ZERO divisor, whose H1 has dimension genus C at every field extension), so H1(C_B,F)=0, H0 finite projective, H0 stalk rank 1 at every prime. pic-g's htriv_of_pic0 then removes its binder entirely.
 (e) picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn -- unit local equations present the TRIVIAL class, generic in the scheme, no curve/ring/degree/cohomology. Only producer in the tree that ESTABLISHES rather than transports triviality (verified by census, not grep). It closes the degree-0 certified chain at CechPic level, where divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero stopped at the DivFam quotient.

STILL OWED, and unowned: hrigAff has NO producer. Field-point separation is not implied by the landed separation results -- PicEtAff.unit_injective and relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover are separation along ETALE COVERS, and a field point is not one unless A is already a field (audited as correct). The cheapest refutation site for hrigAff, unchecked by anyone: A = the zero ring, where the antecedent is vacuous.

TWO PRICING CORRECTIONS OTHER LANES SHOULD READ. (i) The evaluation map pi^*pi_*L -> L IS in mathlib -- the counit of Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction, applied in the sibling in two files. My earlier absolute was false and unmeasured. The defensible residue is that no theorem says the counit is an ISO at a sheaf of this kind, and AJCR's carriers are not Scheme.Modules, so reaching it is a port. (ii) The bookkeeping in Pic0RigidityAffineReduction is NOT what carries its headline (which also follows from pre-session material); what it buys is the general-T form."

Both spellings of the surviving ring-case obligation reduce to a finite covering family of localizations, using only the SEPARATION half of the landed Zariski sheaf property (PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq); nothing is glued. Then PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime / rigidity_of_forall_prime remove the cover from the STATEMENT: a basic-open neighbourhood at each prime suffices, via Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (compactness of Spec A). jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton and _rigidity compose that to the goal object, so the whole vanishing route now has a shortest form: a LOCAL computation of the plus construction at each prime of each test algebra, nothing else.

(2) THE DEGENERATE SITE IS SETTLED, and it went the opposite way to the fear. hrigAff antecedent is vacuous at a subsingleton test ring, which made it the cheapest potential refutation site (I-1655, recorded as unchecked). PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton proves the CONCLUSION holds there anyway, unconditionally: Spec of a subsingleton ring is empty, so the product is, so CechPic and relPic are trivial, and every etale cover of a subsingleton ring is again subsingleton. So the affine spelling is SATISFIED at that site, not refuted.

(3) COMPUTING Pic ON A TWO-CHART COVER IS COMPUTING UNIT GROUPS. Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean. The Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of the two-chart comparison and never composed them; the composite turns a fact about the unit groups of THREE RINGS into triviality of a Picard class, general in the scheme.

(4) Pic(P1_A) = Z OVER A DOMAIN, both directions. Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean, mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff. AND the finding that runs against my own (3): not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits shows the UNIVERSAL hypothesis of (3) is FALSE at P1 -- t is not a coboundary. Repaired in place by cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary, which constrains only the PRESENTING units and is a proved weakening. THE RESIDUE, exactly, and it is NOT the quantifier any more: NO DEGREE MAP EXISTS on the two-chart Cech Picard group. Searched, absent. MEASURED, so nobody re-runs it: local does NOT imply seminormal. Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A) IS available for local A (mathlib CommRing.Pic.instSubsingletonOfFiniteMaximalSpectrum) but Subsingleton (Pic (Polynomial A)) does NOT follow from IsLocalRing A -- exact? fails. Seminormality is absent from mathlib. So (1) moves the obligation to local rings and does not discharge it there."

   251	\begin{definition}[The colength certificate of degree \(n\)]
   252	  \label{def:isCertified}
   253	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified}
   254	  \uses{def:gluedColength}
   255	  \leanok
   256	  \source{kleiman-picard}
   257	  A finite chart adaptation \(A\) is \emph{certified of degree \(n\)} if
   258	  \begin{enumerate}
   259	    \item[(c1)] every chart colength module \(Q_j\) is finite and projective over \(R\);
   260	    \item[(c2)] the glued colength module \(W(A)\) is finite and projective over \(R\), and
   261	      has constant rank \(n\) at every prime: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathfrak p} W(A) = n\)
   262	      for all \(\mathfrak p \in \Spec R\);
   263	    \item[(c3)] the cokernel of the inclusion \(W(A) \hookrightarrow \prod_j Q_j\) is flat
   264	      over \(R\);
   265	    \item[(c4)] the cokernel of \(\delta^- - \delta^+\) is flat over \(R\).
   266	  \end{enumerate}
   267	  Clauses (c1) and (c2) say that the divisor is finite flat of degree \(n\) over the base
   268	  --- Kleiman's condition that a relative effective divisor of degree \(n\) have
   269	  \(S\)-flat structure sheaf with fibres of length \(n\). Clauses (c3) and (c4) are what
   270	  make the certificate stable under an \emph{arbitrary} base change \(R \to R'\): they are
   271	  the flatness hypotheses under which tensoring the defining left-exact sequence
   272	  \(0 \to W(A) \to \prod_j Q_j \to \prod_{ij} Q_{ij}\) with \(R'\) stays exact, so that the
   273	  base-changed glued module is again the equalizer of the base-changed arrows. Over a field
   274	  they are automatic.
   275	\end{definition}

   308	\section{The Zariski-local certificate}
   309	\label{sec:divfamzar}
   310	
   311	The certificate of \ref{def:isCertified} is a condition on \emph{global} modules over
   312	\(R\), and it is genuinely restrictive: it forces the divisor to sit, chart-trace by
   313	chart-trace, in a closed way inside the two pinned charts. The next theorem is that
   314	obstruction, and it is the reason the functor of Section~\ref{sec:divfam} is not the one
   315	the representability argument uses.

   326	  of points at which the equation of \(d\) is not a unit.

   329	      \(R\)-module if and only if \(\operatorname{Supp}(d) \cap P_j\) is closed in \(C_R\)
   330	      --- that is, iff the support does not \emph{leak} out of the piece.

   332	      pinned-chart traces \(\operatorname{Supp}(d) \cap V_0^R\) and
   333	      \(\operatorname{Supp}(d) \cap V_1^R\) are closed in \(C_R\).

   335	      certified adaptation in any degree; and if some representative of a divisor class has

   337	      \(V_1^R\), then \emph{no} representative of that class admits one.

   339	\end{theorem}

1	\chapter{The divisor scheme and the representability of \(\mathrm{Pic}^0\)}
     2	\label{chap:DivisorScheme}
     3	
     4	Grothendieck's construction of the Picard scheme does not represent \(\mathrm{Pic}\)
     5	directly. It represents first the functor of relative effective divisors, and then
     6	presents \(\mathrm{Pic}\) as a quotient of that divisor scheme along the Abel map: the
     7	Abel map is a surjection of sheaves whose fibres are linear systems, and a scheme
     8	representing \(\mathrm{Pic}\) is obtained by descending along it
     9	(\ref{def:localEquations_picClass}, and Kleiman's Theorem 4.8 and its proof).
    10	
    11	This chapter builds the divisor half of that argument for the curve \(C/k\) of
    12	Chapter~\ref{chap:Challenge}, in the form in which the representability seam
    13	\ref{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts} can consume it. The three steps are:
    14	
    15	\begin{enumerate}
    16	  \item a functor \(\Div^{\,n}_{C/k}\) of degree-\(n\) relative divisors, defined on affine
    17	    test algebras by \emph{local equations plus a finite chart adaptation carrying a
    18	    colength certificate}, and its Zariski-localised form (Sections
    19	    \ref{sec:divfam}--\ref{sec:divfamzar});
    20	  \item an embedding \(\varepsilon\) of that functor into a product of two Grassmannians,
    21	    sending a divisor \(D\) to the pair of window submodules
    22	    \(H^0(\OO(aF - D)) \subseteq H^0(\OO(aF))\) at two pinned exponents \(a\), and a closed
    23	    subscheme \(\mathbf{Div}\) of that Grassmannian pair carved out by the multiplication
    24	    condition which the image satisfies (Section~\ref{sec:divscheme}); this is
    25	    Grothendieck's embedding of a Quot-type functor into a Grassmannian by a twisted
    26	    pushforward;
    27	  \item the \emph{backward} half of representability --- every divisor class over an affine
    28	    test induces a unique morphism to \(\mathbf{Div}\), and the class is recoverable from
    29	    that morphism (Section~\ref{sec:divclassify}).
    30	\end{enumerate}
    31	
    32	The forward half --- a universal divisor family on \(\mathbf{Div}\) --- is not built here.
    33	Section~\ref{sec:divrep} states exactly what it must be, derives the affine equivalence and
    34	the chart family of \ref{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts} from it, and isolates the
    35	unproved statement (\ref{thm:divRepUniversalFamily}).
    36	
    37	Throughout, \(k\) is a field, \(C\) is a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over
    38	\(k\) of genus \(g\), \(\pi \colon C \to \PP^1_k\) is a finite dominant morphism, and
    39	\(F\) is its fibre Weil divisor (\ref{def:fiberWeilDivisor}). For a \(k\)-algebra \(R\) we
    40	write \(C_R\) for the relative curve (\ref{def:relCurve}) and \(V_0^R, V_1^R\) for the two
    41	pinned charts of \(C_R\) obtained by pulling back the two standard charts of \(\PP^1\)
    42	along \(\pi\) (\ref{def:relCover}, \ref{def:fiberTwoCover}). We abbreviate
    43	\(H_a := H^0(C, \OO(aF))\) (\ref{def:divisorSections}).

    45	\section{Divisor equality of local-equation systems}
   118	\section{The relative divisor functor of the curve}
   119	\label{sec:divfam}
   120	
   121	Fix a \(k\)-algebra \(R\). A relative effective divisor on \(C_R/R\) is, locally on
   122	\(C_R\), cut out by one equation which is regular on the fibres; a local-equation system on
   123	\(C_R\) records exactly that, but on an \emph{arbitrary} pointed cover, and with regularity
   124	asked in the stalks of \(C_R\) rather than on the fibres. Two further data turn a
   125	local-equation system into a value of a functor with a finite presentation: a refinement of
   126	its cover by finitely many basic opens of the two pinned charts, and a certificate
   127	asserting that the resulting colength modules are finite projective over \(R\) of constant
   128	rank \(n\). The certificate is what plays the role of \(R\)-flatness with fibres of degree
   129	\(n\) in Kleiman's Definition of \(\Div^{\,n}_{X/S}\).
   130	
   131	\begin{definition}[Finite chart cover data]
   132	  \label{def:finCoverData}
   133	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData, AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.pieces,
   134	    AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.cover₀, AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.cover₁,
   135	    AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces,
   136	    AlgebraicGeometry.le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one}
   137	  \uses{def:relCurve, def:relCover, def:fiberTwoCover}
   138	  \leanok
   139	  \emph{Finite chart cover data} on \(C_R\) consists of finitely many sections
   140	  \(h^0_1,\dots,h^0_{m_0} \in \struct{}(V_0^R)\) and \(h^1_1,\dots,h^1_{m_1} \in
   141	  \struct{}(V_1^R)\), together with coefficients \(a^\iota_j\) in the same rings satisfying
   142	  the two partition identities
   143	  \[
   144	    \sum_{j} a^0_j h^0_j = 1 \ \text{ in } \struct{}(V_0^R), \qquad
   145	    \sum_{j} a^1_j h^1_j = 1 \ \text{ in } \struct{}(V_1^R).
   146	  \]
   147	  Its \emph{pieces} are the basic opens \(P_j := D(h^\iota_j) \subseteq V_\iota^R\), indexed
   148	  by the disjoint union of the two index sets. Each piece is affine, and the pieces of each
   149	  chart cover that chart:
   150	  \(V_0^R = \bigcup_j D(h^0_j)\) and \(V_1^R = \bigcup_j D(h^1_j)\).
   151	\end{definition}
   152	\begin{proof}
   153	  \leanok
   154	  A basic open of an affine open is affine, and the pinned charts are affine over the
   155	  base, so each \(P_j\) is affine.
   156	
   157	  For the covering claim on \(V_0^R\): let \(z \in V_0^R\) and suppose \(z \notin D(h^0_j)\)
   158	  for every \(j\), that is, the germ of every \(h^0_j\) at \(z\) lies in the maximal ideal
   159	  of \(\struct{C_R, z}\). Taking germs at \(z\) in the partition identity gives
   160	  \(1 = \sum_j (a^0_j)_z (h^0_j)_z\), which exhibits \(1\) as an element of the maximal
   161	  ideal --- impossible in a local ring. Hence some \(h^0_j\) is a unit at \(z\), i.e.\
   162	  \(z \in D(h^0_j)\). The same argument applies on \(V_1^R\).
   163	\end{proof}

   165	\begin{definition}[Finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system]
   166	  \label{def:divisorAdaptation}
   167	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation, AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors}

   172	  \(\mathcal U\). A \emph{finite chart adaptation} \(A\) of \(d\) consists of finite chart
   173	  cover data (\ref{def:finCoverData}) with pieces \(P_j\), together with sections
   174	  \(f_j \in \struct{}(P_j)\) subject to the \emph{refinement clause}: for every piece index
   175	  \(j\) and every point \(y \in C_R\) there is a unit
   176	  \(u \in \struct{}(P_j \cap \mathcal U(y))^{\times}\) with
   177	  \[
   178	    f_j\big|_{P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)} \;=\; u \cdot d_y\big|_{P_j \cap \mathcal U(y)} .
   179	  \]

   180	  (The quantifier ranges over \emph{all} \(y\); over an empty overlap the section ring is
   181	  the zero ring and the clause is vacuous.)

   201	\begin{lemma}[The adapted equations are regular]
   202	  \label{lem:divisorAdaptation_eqn_regular}

    11	
    12	The certificate of `informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §4.1: `DivScheme g` is delivered
    13	quasi-projective **as consumed** — the closed immersion `divSchemeι` into the
    14	Grassmannian pair together with the pair's finite affine frame atlas, quasi-compactness,
    15	local finite-typeness over `k`, and separatedness, and the same three properties derived
    16	on `DivScheme g` itself (closed immersions into qc/lft/separated transfer).
    17	
    18	## The Grassmannian-pair data (§4.1 middle factor)
    19	
    20	* `Grassmannian.isAffine_grPairCover_X`: each patch of the finite product atlas
    21	  `grPairCover` is affine (with `finite_grPairCover_index`, `GrassmannianPair.lean:68`:
    22	  the **finite affine frame atlas**).
    23	* `Grassmannian.compactSpace_grPair`, `quasiCompact_grPairStructMap`: quasi-compactness
    24	  is FREE — finitely many affine charts glue to a compact space; no image argument.
    25	* `Grassmannian.locallyOfFiniteType_grPairStructMap`: charts are `Spec` of finite-type
    26	  `k`-algebras (DD-3's `locallyOfFiniteType_grStructMap`), stable under base change and
    27	  composition through the pair.
    28	* `Grassmannian.isSeparated_grPairStructMap`, `isSeparated_grPair`: the GRQ
    29	  affine-diagonal argument (DD-3's `isSeparated_grStructMap`) through the pullback.
    30	
    31	## The derived bundle on `DivScheme g` (§4.2 consumer rows)
    32	
    33	* `quasiCompact_carveSchemeOverHom` / `quasiCompact_divSchemeOverHom` and
    34	  `compactSpace_carveScheme` / `compactSpace_divScheme`: the **Wave-5 qc inputs**
    35	  toward `AbelSourceData.isProper` (`AbelianVariety/AbelSource.lean`).
    36	* `locallyOfFiniteType_carveSchemeOverHom` / `locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom`:
    37	  the **DAT-glue lft certificate** for the 01JJ chart family.
    38	* `isSeparated_carveSchemeOverHom` / `isSeparated_divSchemeOverHom` and
    39	  `isSeparated_carveScheme` / `isSeparated_divScheme`: separatedness over `k` and
    40	  absolute — with lft and qc, the `IsProper` constituents short of universal closedness.
    41	* `DivQProjBundle` / `divQProj`: the §4.1 bundle verbatim, the single citable
    42	  certificate for **DAT-G**'s quasi-projective charts.
    43	
    44	## Honest boundary (§4.1, BINDING)
    45	
    46	PROJECTIVITY of the Grassmannian (Plücker) is **not** delivered — nothing here is an
    47	ample bundle or a valuative/universal-closedness certificate.  "Quasi-projective" is
    48	consumed as the bundle above; if a consumer needs honest projectivity (or universal
    49	closedness of `grPair`, e.g. for the properness of `Div^g` feeding

{
  "id": "AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.finite-field-avoid",
  "status": "pending",
  "priority": "high",
  "owner": "",
  "title": "Finite-field avoidance: bound fibre support by g and avoid it after a large finite extension",
  "summary": "*** PROTECTION CONFLICT in this row's REMAINING clause, flagged review-ajcr r7 (2026-07-30). This row is pending at HIGH priority, so it reads as the next thing to do -- and the work it names is forbidden. ***

STATE: 2 of 3 children DONE. finite-field-avoid.cardinality (e602378af) proves the exact finite-cardinality P1 avoidance theorem under S.ncard + 2 <= card(k). finite-field-avoid.support-degree (d6c67f41d) builds the pointwise seed residue equations with no certificate and no hproj, and bounds their support by g points.

THE REMAINING CLAUSE AS WRITTEN IS FORBIDDEN. It said the third child 'must choose a large finite Galois extension, transport P1 twists and fixed-twist divisor charts through scalar extension, and descend the semilinear outer atlas', depending on the twist-atlas architecture. Human decision I-0492 clause 1 forbids both halves -- the GL_2(k)/Aut(P1) action on P1 (twistedP1Map = pi >> P1.autOfMatrix) and descent work whose only purpose is to rescue R1 -- and twist-atlas is REJECTED on exactly that ground. See the descent leaf for the full flag.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT, and it is smaller than the clause implies: the descent leaf's FIRST sentence only -- transport the residue support into P1(k), combine image-ncard injectivity with the ncard <= g bound and the (done) finite-cardinality theorem, and spread the fibre containment to a support tube. No twist, no Galois descent, and both its inputs are done.

WHY THE PRICE MOVED IN THE GOOD DIRECTION: the twist quantifier this row was trying to absorb with an outer atlas simply does not occur on the widened carrier -- IsLocallyCertifiedAff, DivFamZarAff and divFunctorAff take (C, R, n) and no pi. So finite-field avoidance does not owe an atlas; it owes the endpoint assembly.

Priority left high on the assembly, which is legitimate and unclaimed."
}
